newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP backs proposals on banks and investment firms.
newsitem.headline: EP backs proposals on banks and investment firms.

text.p: The European Parliament has approved plans to improve controls on banks and investment companies.

On Thursday Euro-MPs gave a first reading to a proposal to make technical amendments to three European Union directives on banking -- the 1997 banking directive, the 1989 solvability directive and the 1993 directive on capital adequacy.

The aim of the proposal -- COM(96)183 -- is to enable EU member states to make information exchange agreements with supervisory authorities in third countries and, in the case of the solvency directive, to allow for a lower risk weighting.

Parliament on Wednesday gave a second reading to another proposal. This provides for the creation of a securities committee to help the European Commission monitor two EU directives on the capital requirements of investment companies operating in the single market.
Euro-MPs introduced several amendments to the draft directive -- COM(96)292 -- which aim to reduce national governments' powers on the committee and increase the role played by the parliament.
Both proposals must have the approval of Euro-MPs and the EU Council of Ministers to become law.
